An external reference of no more than 1.2 V can be applied between SDADC_REF (P0_16) and SDADC_GND (P0_06) for better precision.

Set SDADC_CTRL_REG[SDADC_EN]; set the GPIO to Px_yy_MODE_REG[PID] = 26; choose the positive input (SDADC_INP_SEL) and negative input (SDADC_INN_SEL, ignored single-ended); choose the reference (SDADC_VREF_SEL), single-ended or differential, and manual or continuous (SDADC_CONT); set other options; start with SDADC_START and wait for it to clear or for the interrupt; clear the interrupt by writing SDADC_CLEAR_INT_REG; read SDADC_RESULT_REG.

Present on DA14691, DA14695, DA14697 and DA14699. The audio unit has a PDM and a PCM interface and a sample rate converter (SRC) between them and memory. It converts 32-bit SRC_IN to 32-bit SRC_OUT, 1-bit PDM_IN to SRC_OUT, and SRC_IN to 1-bit PDM_OUT, at SRC sample rates of 8 kHz to 192 kHz with SNR above 100 dB. I/O is single-buffered and DMA capable; an automatic mode tracks an incoming frame sync such as PCM_FSC, a manual mode interrupts at the programmed rate and software adjusts from the buffer pointers. The audio streams have their own DMA channels, and PCM also has an 8 × 32-bit FIFO, unusable in stereo mode.

The PCM interface is synchronous, up to 192 kHz, master or slave, for audio devices, ISDN circuits and serial data. PCM_FSC runs from 4 kHz to 96 kHz in master or slave, with a strobe length of 1, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48 or 64 bits; in master mode it can lead the first bit or coincide with it. It carries 2 × 32 channels, with a programmable slot delay up to 31 × 8 bits, in PCM, I2S (left/right selection, N × 8 bits each side) and IOM2 (two clocks per bit) formats, with clock and frame sync inversion.

The PDM interface connects one stereo or two mono devices (for example MEMS microphones, or outputs) over one clock, PDM_CLK, and one data line carrying two channels time-multiplexed. PDM_CLK runs from 62.5 kHz to 4 MHz and can be stopped for sleep; data is down-sampled to 32 bits in the SRC. Input is one channel in stereo format; output is two channels in mono format or one in stereo. Left/right selection is programmable.

The SRC handles two 32-bit channels, treated as one stereo pair or as two separate mono streams. PCM data pairs go to SRC1_IN1/2 and come out left-aligned on SRC1_OUT1/2; the two 1-bit PDM inputs arrive on PDM_IN and become 2 × 32 bits left-aligned on SRC_OUT. APU_MUX_REG[PDM1_MUX_IN] selects the SRC input from the interfaces or SRC1_IN1/2_REG, whose bits 31-8 map to SRC bits 23-0. SRC outputs are read in SRC1_OUT1_REG and SRC1_OUT2_REG or routed to PCM by APU_MUX_REG[PCM1_MUX_IN]. Outside stereo mode an 8 × 32-bit FIFO can sit on the SRC input (SRC_IN_IRQ when it reaches four samples) or output (SRC_OUT_IRQ when it drops below five), or be disabled. In manual mode the rates are set in SRC1_IN_FS_REG and SRC1_OUT_FS_REG; in automatic mode they follow the external sync and are only read back there. With PDM the SRC runs in automatic mode and SRC1_IN_FS_REG reports PDM_CLK/64, 64 being the default oversampling ratio. The up/down sampler resamples arbitrarily by polynomial interpolation at 8x oversampled input and 16x oversampled output rate, on a single-cycle multiplier with optional pre and post adders.

TX and RX each have two 32-bit registers (PCM1_IN1/OUT1_REG, PCM1_IN1/OUT2_REG), arranged as eight 8-bit channels; clock inversion, channel delay and strobe length give PCM, I2S, TDM and IOM2. PCM1_CTRL_REG[PCM_CH_DEL] delays the channels by up to 31 × 8 bits; a long delay with a slow clock can let PCM_FSC arrive before all channels have shifted, misaligning the current channel. PCM_CLK comes from the system clock by a fractional divider (integer in the 12-bit PCM_DIV_REG[PCM_DIV], fraction in the 16-bit PCM_FDIV_REG, which adds jitter) or integer only (extra clock pulses beyond the word are ignored, for slaves that cannot take jitter). In PCM_FDIV_REG the position of the highest 1 gives the denominator and the number of 1s the numerator. PCM_FSC is PCM_CLK divided by PCM_FSC_DIV.

In slave mode the PCM interface can feed the SRC directly, so a drifting PCM_FSC or another frame rate such as 44.1 kHz can be resampled to, for example, 48 kHz inside. Master mode is PCM1_CTRL_REG[PCM_MASTER] = 1: PCM_FSC is an output over channel 0, high for PCM_FSCLEN = 1 or 8, 16, 24 or 32 clocks, with PCM_FSCDEL placing it ahead of channel 0's first bit or on it, repeating at 8 to 192 kHz set by PCM_FSC_DIV. PCM_CLK is an output with one or two clocks per bit (PCM_CLK_BIT; with 1 the FSC length doubles), invertible by PCM_CLKINV. In slave mode PCM_FSC is an input marking channel 0; its rate equals PCM_SYNC, and it is high at least one PCM_CLK cycle and low at least one cycle per frame; PCM_FSCDEL places it before or on the MSB. PCM_CLK is then an input from 256 kHz to 12.288 MHz, and a rising edge on PCM1_FSC or PCM2_FSC can halt or restart the main counter.

The interface supports I2S, left-justified, right-justified and TDM formats. In I2S mode the right channel's MSB is valid on the second rising bit-clock edge after PCM_FSC rises and the left channel's on the second after it falls. In TDM mode the left channel's data is valid PCM_CH_DEL clocks after PCM_FSC rises and the right channel's the same delay after it falls; delaying the channels gives left or right alignment; the offset is always a multiple of 8. In IOM format PCM_CLK runs at twice the bit rate; in slave mode PCM_FSC's first rising edge gives the sync, and input data is taken on the second falling clock edge.

PDM data carries the left channel on the falling edge of the clock and the right channel on the rising edge; in mono only one channel is present. Stopping PDM_CLK puts MEMS microphones into sleep. PDM data and clock can be placed on any GPIO with PID = 32 and PID = 33 in Px_yz_MODE_REG. Audio quality degrades below an oversampling ratio of 64: at 8 kHz the PDM clock should be at least 64 × 8 kHz = 512 kHz.

When more than one sample moves at a time, or the rate would interrupt the CPU too often, DMA is used; three DMA channels are reserved for PCM, SRC input and SRC output. After each conversion the up-sampler on the input side and the down-sampler on the output side give edge-triggered interrupts SRC_IN_SYNC and SRC_OUT_SYNC that need no clearing; only one sample is read or written per register at a time.

operation.topic: Audio unit setup, PDM in to PCM out
operation.text: Set the GPIOs to PID 32 and 33 (PDM) and 28 to 31 (PCM) and their direction. PDM: master (PDM_DIV_REG[PDM_MASTER_MODE]), clock divider PDM_DIV, clock enable CLK_PDM_EN. PCM, sizing PCM_FSC_DIV and PCM_FSCLEN from the actual word size: clock source PCM_SRC_SEL, dividers PCM_DIV and PCM_FDIV_REG, CLK_PCM_EN, PCM_EN = 0, then PCM1_CTRL_REG fields PCM_FSC_DIV, PCM_FSC_EDGE, PCM_CH_DEL, PCM_CLK_BIT, PCM_FSCINV, PCM_CLKINV, PCM_PPOD (DO output mode), PCM_FSCDEL, PCM_FSCLEN and PCM_MASTER = 1. SRC: divider SRC_DIV, CLK_SRC_EN, input filter SRC_IN_DS and rate SRC1_IN_FS_REG, output filter SRC_OUT_US and rate SRC1_OUT_FS_REG, APU_MUX_REG[PDM1_MUX_IN] = 1, SRC FIFO enabled with SRC_FIFO_DIRECTION = 1 (not in stereo), APU_MUX_REG[PCM1_MUX_IN] = 1, APU_MUX_REG[SRC1_MUX_IN] = 0, SRC_IN_AMODE = 1. Then SRC_EN = 1 and PCM_EN = 1.

Present on DA14691, DA14695, DA14697 and DA14699. A two-wire bus controller (SDA data, SCL clock) for standard mode (0 to 100 kbit/s), fast mode (up to 400 kbit/s) and high-speed mode (up to 3.4 Mbit/s). It has transmit and receive FIFOs 32 entries deep (receive 32 x 8 bits, transmit 32 x 10 bits), master transmit and master receive, 7-bit or 10-bit addressing and combined-format transfers in either, bulk transmit, clock synchronisation, a programmable SDA hold time, interrupt or polled operation, waiting on bits and bytes at either speed, and DMA. The default slave address is 0x055.

Inside are an APB bus interface to the register file, master and slave state machines, a clock generator (SCL generation as master, bus-idle check, START and STOP generation, data set-up and hold), receive and transmit shifters, a receive filter that detects START, STOP and lost arbitration, toggle and synchroniser logic that carry signals between clock domains, an interrupt controller, and the two FIFOs with their level status.

Software sets the controller as a master. A transfer opens with START or RESTART, the slave address and a read/write bit; the receiver of each byte returns ACK. A master reading from a slave ends with NACK on the last byte followed by STOP, or RESTART to address another slave. SDA changes only while SCL is low except at START, STOP and RESTART. The drivers are open-drain so the lines wire-AND; only the 400 pF maximum bus capacitance caps how many devices may be attached. Several masters may share the bus.

operation.topic: I2C START, STOP and combined formats
operation.text: As master, writing data into the transmit FIFO makes the controller issue START. Setting bit 9 of I2C_DATA_CMD_REG issues STOP; without it no STOP is sent even when the FIFO runs empty. As a slave the controller never issues START or STOP; on a read request it holds SCL low until read data is supplied or the slave is disabled (I2C_ENABLE = 0). With I2C_CON.I2C_RESTART_EN = 1 the master uses a combined format (RESTART) whenever the next queued transfer changes direction; if the FIFO is empty at the end of a transfer it sends STOP and the next transfer starts with START. Mixing a 7-bit and a 10-bit address transaction in one combined format is not supported.

Idle bus: both lines pulled high by external pull-up resistors. START is SDA falling while SCL is high; STOP is SDA rising while SCL is high. SDA must stay stable while SCL is high during data. The edges are those at the master's outputs; unequal line delays can change the SDA/SCL relationship seen at a slave.

7-bit format: bits 7:1 of the first byte are the slave address and bit 0 is R/W (0 = master writes, 1 = master reads). 10-bit format: two address bytes; the first carries 11110 in bits 7:3, address bits 9:8 in bits 2:1 and R/W in bit 0, the second carries address bits 7:0. The controller does not prevent use of the reserved addresses, which may clash with other I2C devices.

Master-transmitter: bytes are sent with no limit on count; the slave-receiver acknowledges the address and each byte; if it fails to ACK, the master aborts with STOP, the slave leaving SDA high. Master-receiver: the master ACKs every byte except the last, which it NACKs; the slave then releases SDA so the master can send STOP. Instead of STOP the master may send RESTART (a START after the ACK pulse) and talk to the same or another slave.

For slaves without I2C hardware that poll the bus, the master can open every transfer with a START byte: START, the byte 0000 0001, a dummy ACK clock that no slave pulls low, then RESTART. The polling device under-samples until it sees a 0 and then switches to the master's rate. Addressed as a slave, the controller always samples at its highest speed and never needs a START byte.

operation.topic: I2C multi-master arbitration and clock synchronisation
operation.text: Arbitration happens on SDA while SCL is high: a master sending 1 while another sends 0 loses and turns off its data output, though it may keep clocking to the end of the byte. Two masters addressing the same slave can arbitrate into the data phase. In high-speed mode each master has a unique 8-bit master code (I2C_HS_MADDR), so arbitration ends within the code. There is no central master or priority order. Arbitration is not allowed between RESTART and a data bit, STOP and a data bit, or RESTART and STOP; slaves take no part. SCL is synchronised by its wired-AND: whichever master's high time is shortest pulls SCL low first, and the master whose low time is longest holds the others in a high wait state. Slaves may hold SCL low to slow the bus.

1. Map the pins: Px_yy_MODE_REG[PID] = 21 to 24. 2. Speed, with CLK_COM_REG[I2Cx_CLK_SEL] = 0 (DivN clock): I2Cx_CON_REG[I2C_SPEED] = 1 for standard (100 kbit/s), 2 for full speed (400 kbit/s), 3 for high speed (1 Mbit/s). 3. Master: I2C_MASTER_MODE = 1 and I2C_SLAVE_DISABLE = 1; slave: both 0. 4. Choose 7- or 10-bit addressing (I2C_10BITADDR_MASTER, I2C_10BITADDR_SLAVE). 5. Target address I2Cx_TAR_REG[IC_TAR] (master) or own address I2Cx_SAR_REG[IC_SAR] (slave), both 0x55 by default. 6. FIFO thresholds I2Cx_RX_TL_REG and I2Cx_TX_TL_REG. 7. Interrupt mask I2Cx_INTR_MASK_REG. 8. Enable with CLK_COM_REG[I2Cx_ENABLE]. To read a byte write I2C_CMD = 1 to I2Cx_DATA_CMD_REG; to write one write I2C_CMD = 0 with the byte in I2C_DAT; then wait for TFE = 1 and MST_ACTIVITY = 0 in I2Cx_STATUS_REG.

Present on DA14691, DA14695, DA14697 and DA14699. Three 16550-compatible UARTs: UART, UART2 and UART3. Each has 16-byte transmit and 16-byte receive FIFOs and DMA. UART2 and UART3 add RTS/CTS hardware flow control and a 9-bit mode; UART3 adds ISO 7816 support. Characters have 5 to 8 data bits, optional odd or even parity and 1, 1.5 or 2 stop bits; break generation and detection, prioritised interrupt identification, shadow registers with a software reset, and a programmable THRE interrupt mode are included. The baud divisor has a fractional part UART_DLF/16.

A character is a start bit, the data bits LSB first, the optional parity bit and the stop bits; every bit except the half stop bit of a 1.5-stop setting lasts one bit time, which is 16 baud clocks. After the start bit is detected, the receiver samples each bit near its middle, every 16 baud clocks from the mid-point of the start bit. The baud rate is set by the serial clock and the divisor latch (DLH, DLL); an optional baud clock output (baudout_n) is part of the 16550 set.

Each UART runs on two clocks, pclk for the APB interface and an asynchronous serial clock sclk for the baud rate, with a synchroniser between them. A serial clock more than four times pclk leaves too little time to push a received character into the FIFO. After configuration, nothing should be sent or received for up to eight cycles of the slower clock while the serial-clock logic picks up the new register values.

operation.topic: UART interrupts and programmable THRE mode
operation.text: UART_INT is raised by any enabled interrupt type: receiver error, receiver data available, character timeout (FIFO mode only) and transmitter holding register empty at or below threshold. Software reads UART_IIR_REG for the source. With programmable THRE mode enabled (IER[7]) and the FIFOs on, the THRE interrupt fires at and below a transmit FIFO threshold set in FCR[5:4] (empty, 2, a quarter or a half) instead of only at empty, and LSR[5] then reports FIFO full instead of FIFO empty, so software can top up the FIFO by polling LSR[5]. Disabling the FIFOs with FCR[0] also disables this mode.

operation.topic: UART shadow registers and direct test mode
operation.text: Shadow registers avoid read-modify-write: UART_SRBR_REG and UART_STHR give burst access to the receive buffer and transmit holding register at incrementing addresses; UART_SFE_REG, UART_SRT_REG and UART_STER_REG reach FCR[0], FCR[7:6] and FCR[5:4] alone. The UARTs can carry Bluetooth LE direct test mode for PHY testing, either over HCI with a full CTS/RTS UART or over a 2-wire UART.

1. Map the pins: Px_yy_MODE_REG[PID] = 1 to 10. 2. For UART2/3 choose the clock with CLK_COM_REG[UART2/3_CLK_SEL] (not needed for UART). 3. Enable with CLK_COM_REG[UARTx_ENABLE]. 4. Set UARTx_LCR_REG[UART_DLAB] to reach the divisor latches. 5. Write the divisor: integer high byte to UARTx_IER_DLH_REG, low byte to UARTx_RBR_THR_DLL_REG, fraction to UARTx_DLF_REG. 6. Break, parity, stop bits and data length in UARTx_LCR_REG. 7. FIFO in UARTx_IIR_FCR_REG. 8. Interrupts in UARTx_IER_DLH_REG. To send, wait for UART_THRE, write the byte to UARTx_RBR_THR_DLL_REG and check UART_TEMT; to receive, wait for UART_DR and read UARTx_RBR_THR_DLL_REG.

Present on DA14691, DA14695, DA14697 and DA14699. UART3 carries an asynchronous smart card interface to ISO/IEC 7816-3 class B and C: a UART line with flow control signals, an interrupt line, DMA, an error signal that marks a character for repetition, inverse and direct convention, and guard time.

The ISO 7816-3 clock is derived from the system clock with a 50 % duty cycle. ISO7816_CLK_DIV in UART3_CTRL_REG may be changed whether or not the clock runs; ISO7816_CLK_STATUS shows whether it runs, clearing ISO7816_CLK_EN stops it, and ISO7816_CLK_LEVEL gives the level it holds while stopped.

operation.topic: Smart card timer and guard time
operation.text: The ISO 7816-3 timer has two modes set by UART3_TIMER_REG[ISO7816_TIM_MODE]. Mode 0: clocked by the ISO 7816 clock, it starts when ISO7816_TIM_EN = 1, counts from 0 to ISO7816_TIM_MAX, then stops and sets ISO7816_TIM_EXPIRED_IRQ (an interrupt if ISO7816_TIM_EXPIRED_IRQMASK = 1), cleared by setting ISO7816_TIM_EN. Mode 1: clocked at 1/16 of the UART bit clock (1/16 etu; not a fixed rate when the fractional divider is used), it restarts from 0 at each transmitted start bit. With ISO_TIM_MAX = 16 × guard time - 1 it times the minimum gap between leading edges of consecutive characters: for a guard time over 12 etu, its expiry permits the next character in non-FIFO mode, and in FIFO mode ISO7816_AUTO_GT sends the next character automatically.

Follows section 7.3 of ISO 7816-3. Transmitting, the block samples the data line 11 etu after a character's leading edge and raises ISO7816_ERR_TX_TIME_IRQ for every character sent and, at the same time, ISO7816_ERR_TX_VALUE_IRQ when the receiver signalled an error; software retransmits on the latter. Receiving, it uses the UART parity check and drives the line low for 1 etu minimum to 2 etu maximum at 10.5 etu; pulse width and offset are set in UART3_ERR_CTRL_REG, and UART_Rx can be held high during the error pulse so the UART flags no error.

1. Map the pins with Px_yy_MODE_REG[PID] = 11 to 12; card reset (output) and card insert (input) are plain GPIOs (PID = 0). 2. CLK_COM_REG[UART3_ENABLE]. 3. UART3 clock CLK_COM_REG[UART3_CLK_SEL]. 4. UART3_CONFIG_REG[ISO7816_ENABLE]. 5. ISO7816_CLK_DIV. 6. Configure UART3: FIFO (the transmit FIFO stays disabled when error detection is on), data length, stop bits, parity enable and even/odd, optional error detection (ISO7816_ERR_SIG_EN with UART3_ERR_CTRL_REG), direct or inverse convention (ISO7816_CONVENTION), the divisor through UART_DLAB, DLH, DLL and DLF, and interrupts in UART3_CTRL_REG. To send: set the guard timer, check FIFO not full (UART_TFNF) or THR empty (UART_THRE), write the byte and check UART_TEMT. To receive: set the wait time in UART3_TIMER_REG, wait for UART_DR or timer expiry, read the byte.

Present on DA14691, DA14695, DA14697 and DA14699. Two instances, SPI and SPI2. Master or slave, 8, 16 or 32-bit words both ways and 9-bit words for transmit as master. The controller clock is up to 32 MHz and the SPI clock output is the source clock divided by 2, 4, 8 or 14, with an SPI clock line rate up to 16 MHz. Modes 0 to 3, programmable SPI_DO idle level, maskable interrupt, write-only and read-only modes that cut bus load, an 8-byte receive and a 4-byte transmit FIFO per block, and DMA.

Master is the default. After the pins are mapped and SPI_CTRL_REG is set, SPI_ON = 1 enables the block. Writing SPI_RX_TX_REG starts a transfer of 8, 9, 16 or 32 clocks, shifting out on SPI_DO and in on SPI_DI; at the end SPI_INT_BIT and SPI_INT_PEND are set and the received word is in SPI_RX_TX_REG. SPI_MINT masks the interrupt and any write to SPI_CLEAR_INT_REG clears it; SPI_INT stays set while the receive FIFO holds unread data. Slave mode: SPI_SMn = 1 with SPI_CLK mapped as input; the internal SPI clock must be at least four times the master's SPI_CLK. SPI_EN is an active-low clock enable and bit synchroniser (SPI_EN_CTRL = 1); de-asserting it mid-word resets the shift buffer. SPI_POL and SPI_PHA set polarity and phase.

As master, SPI_DO idles at the SPI_DO bit value in all modes, and likewise as a slave in modes 0 and 2. In modes 1 and 3 the pin keeps the last LSB after a transfer; pulsing SPI_RST returns it to the SPI_DO bit level (SPI_FORCE_DO also forces it but does not reset the shift buffer).

SPI_FIFO_MODE = 10, write only: only the transmit FIFO is used, received data lands in SPI_RX_TX_REG and is overwritten if not read; SPI_INT is 1 while the FIFO has room, SPI_TXH = 1 when it is full (writing then sends undefined data) and SPI_BUSY falls to 0 when all is sent. SPI_FIFO_MODE = 01, read only: only the receive FIFO is used and, as master, transfers start at once and run until it is full, sending the contents of SPI_TX_REGx (zeros after reset) so no dummy writes are needed. To read exactly N words, read N - fifosize + 1 words, wait for SPI_BUSY = 0, set SPI_FIFO_MODE = 00 and read the last fifosize + 1 words; fifosize is 4, 2 or 1 words for 8, 16 or 32-bit words. SPI_FIFO_MODE = 00: both FIFOs; SPI_TXH means transmit FIFO full and SPI_INT means receive data present.

Without FIFO, an empty transmit buffer raises a DMA transmit request if SPI_DMA_TXREQ_MODE = 1, and an interrupt if SPI_TX_FIFO_NOFULL_MASK = 1. With the transmit FIFO disabled (SPI_FIFO_MODE = 0x3) and SPI_DMA_TXREQ_MODE = 0, the CPU writes one byte to SPI_RX_TX_REG before DMA takes over, and the transmit DMA channel uses edge-sensitive requests (REQ_SENSE = 0x1), or else DMA priority favours the receive channel. With SPI_PRIORITY set, edge-sensitive requests cannot be used and receive-channel priority is the only way to serve both directions. Transmit DMA requests are not supported for 32-bit words with SPI_FIFO_MODE 0x0 or 0x2 (only 8 and 16-bit), nor in receive-only mode 0x1. The 9-bit mode (SPI_WORD = 11) drives 9-bit displays: the ninth bit, from SPI_CTRL_REG1[SPI_9BIT_VAL], marks command or data and leads the word; the FIFOs work as in 8-bit mode and a received ninth bit is discarded.

1. Map the pins: Px_yy_MODE_REG[PID] = 13 to 20. 2. SPI_SMN = 0 for master, 1 for slave (in slave mode also SPI_EN_CTRL). 3. Clock SPI_CLK, phase SPI_PHA, polarity SPI_POL, word size SPI_WORD, FIFO mode SPI_FIFO_MODE. 4. SPI_ON = 1. 5. Assert CS, write SPIx_RX_TX_REG, poll SPI_INT_BIT, read SPIx_RX_TX_REG, clear through SPIx_CLEAR_INT_REG, de-assert CS. To change the configuration: SPI_ON = 0, SPI_RST = 1, update, SPI_ON = 1, SPI_RST = 0, then set SPI_MINT.

Present on DA14691, DA14695, DA14697 and DA14699. Time of day in 12 or 24-hour form with hours, minutes, seconds and hundredths; calendar with day of week, date, month, year, century and leap-year compensation, year 2000 compliant; alarms down to month, date, hour, minute, second and hundredth; an event interrupt on any time or calendar unit; runs during sleep; 10 ms granularity. Years run from 1900 to 2999 and hours 0 to 23 or 1 to 12 with an a.m./p.m. flag.

operation.topic: RTC alarms, events and event controller
operation.text: Alarms are one-time or recurring. Each time and calendar field can raise an event when it rolls over (new month, week, day, half day, minute, second). Alarms and events can interrupt; any interrupt may be masked, enabled, disabled or set whenever wanted. The RTC event controller, stepped every 10 ms or on a roll-over, has a 12-bit down counter reloaded from RTC_MOTOR_EVENT_PERIOD (enable RTC_MOTOR_EVENT_EN) that pulses the motor controller trigger at 0, and a 13-bit down counter reloaded from RTC_PDC_EVENT_PERIOD (enable RTC_PDC_EVENT_EN) that signals the PDC and the Cortex-M33 RTC_EVENT interrupt at 0, cleared by reading RTC_PDC_EVENT_CLEAR_REG. Both counters are readable (RTC_PDC_EVENT_CNT_REG, RTC_MOTOR_EVENT_CNT_REG).

1. For 100 Hz granularity from the LP clock, set CLK_RTCDIV_REG: RTC_DIV_INT to the integer and RTC_DIV_FRAC to the fractional part of FLP_CLK / 100 (for 32768 Hz, 327.680 gives 327 = 0x147 and 680 = 0x2A8), RTC_DIV_DENOM for the fraction's denominator, then RTC_DIV_ENABLE. 2. Clear RTC_TIME_DISABLE and RTC_CAL_DISABLE. 3. Choose 12/24-hour (RTC_HMS). 4. Write RTC_TIME_REG and RTC_CALENDAR_REG. 5. Alarms in RTC_ALARM_ENABLE_REG and RTC_CALENDAR_ALARM_REG, enabled by RTC_ALARM_xxxx_EN. 6. Interrupts with RTC_INTERRUPT_ENABLE_REG / RTC_INTERRUPT_DISABLE_REG, event flags with RTC_EVENT_FLAGS_REG. 7. RTC_KEEP_RTC_REG[RTC_KEEP] chooses whether a software reset resets the RTC. 8. Event controller: for the PDC write the period into RTC_PDC_EVENT_PERIOD_REG then set RTC_PDC_EVENT_EN in RTC_EVENT_CTRL_REG; for the motor controller write RTC_MOTOR_EVENT_PERIOD_REG then set RTC_MOTOR_EVENT_EN.

Present on DA14691, DA14695, DA14697 and DA14699. Four 24-bit timers: Timer and Timer2 in the timers power domain (PD_TMR), Timer3 and Timer4 in the system domain (PD_SYS). Each has PWM output, two GPIO capture inputs (four on Timer), a 5-bit prescaler, a choice of system clock or sleep clock, counting up or down with a free-running option, runs while the system sleeps, and has its own interrupt line (Timer has one more for capture events). One-shot pulses of programmable width are on Timer and Timer2 only. Timer and Timer2 can drive specific GPIOs during sleep.

operation.topic: Timer counter, PWM, capture and one-shot
operation.text: The counter runs on sys_clk or lp_clk through the 5-bit prescaler, from 1 kHz minimum to 32 MHz maximum. The PWM generator, independent of the counter, divides further by up to 2^16 + 1, down to 0.015 kHz; its 16-bit duty value gives 65535 steps. At the lowest PWM frequency only 50 % duty is possible. Frequency and duty registers hold clock counts, and the duty value must stay below the frequency value. A GPIO edge captures the counter into a register and a second GPIO (or the same) captures into another, so their difference measures a period or the interval between two external events. One-shot: a GPIO trigger makes another GPIO output a pulse of programmed width. Timer and Timer2 PWM run in sleep on P1_01 and P1_06 (CLK_TMR_REG[TMR_PWM/2_AON_MODE]).

1. Clear TIM_EN and TIM_CLK_EN. 2. Choose the clock (TIM_SYS_CLK_EN) and prescaler (TIMER_PRESCALER_REG). 3. Set TIM_CLK_EN. 4. Mode (TIM_ONESHOT_MODE_EN). One-shot (Timer, Timer2): delay in TIMER/2_RELOAD_REG, pulse length in TIMER/2_SHOTWIDTH_REG, trigger input TIMER/2_GPIO1_CONF_REG with polarity TIM_IN1_EVENT_FALL_EN, secondary input GPIO2 with TIM_IN2_EVENT_FALL_EN. Counter (all): direction TIM_COUNT_DOWN_EN, reload or maximum in TIMERx_RELOAD_REG, free run TIM_FREE_RUN_MODE_EN when counting up, capture inputs TIMERx_GPIOy_CONF_REG with polarity TIM_INx_EVENT_FALL_EN (up to four on Timer). 5. PWM frequency TIMERx_PWM_FREQ_REG and duty TIMERx_PWM_DC_REG. 6. Capture interrupts TIM_CAP_GPIOy_IRQ_EN. 7. Output pin: Px_yy_MODE_REG[PID] = 3 or 49 to 54. 8. TIM_IRQ_EN. 9. TIM_EN.

Present on DA14691, DA14695, DA14697 and DA14699. Two watchdogs. The system watchdog, in the always-on domain, guards the Cortex-M33: a 13-bit down counter on RC32K (default) or RCX divided by 320, lasting 84 seconds on one clock and three minutes on the other. It raises an NMI at 0 and a hardware reset at -16, has a lock bit against accidental freezing, and freezes automatically while the Cortex-M33 is halted in debug. If RCX is the sleep clock RC32K may be off. The CMAC watchdog, in the radio domain, guards the Cortex-M0+: a 13-bit down counter on lp_clk (XTAL32K or RCX) divided by 32, giving an early interrupt to the Cortex-M0+ at 16, CMAC2SYS_IRQ to the Cortex-M33 at 0 and a hardware reset at -16, with a lock bit and automatic freeze when the Cortex-M0+ is halted in debug. The Cortex-M33 can reach it while the radio domain is powered.

Enabled at power-up and stepped every 10 ms from RC32K. WATCHDOG_REG resets to its maximum, a time-out of 87 seconds, longer on RCX depending on its frequency. Writes must have bits 31-14 at 0, which filters a runaway write of all ones. Past 0 the counter goes negative with bit 13 set: 1, 0, 1FFF (-1), 1FFE (-2) ... 1FF0 (-16). With WATCHDOG_CTRL_REG[NMI_RST] = 0, the NMI comes at 0 and reset at -16 or below, and the NMI handler has 16 x 10 = 160 ms to write a value above -16. With NMI_RST = 1 it resets at 0 or below. The Cortex-M33 can freeze it, and it freezes while the debugger halts the CPU, but it resumes in any sleep mode (PD_SYS off) even if frozen.

Active whenever the radio domain (PD_RAD) is powered. lp_clk / 32 gives a 1 ms period with XTAL32K, so it reaches 0 within 16 ms at most. Interrupt to the Cortex-M0+ at 16, to the Cortex-M33 at 0, hardware reset at -16. CMAC reloads it itself; the Cortex-M33 may freeze or unfreeze it (SET_FREEZE_REG) and reload it (CM_WDOG_REG[CM_WDOG_CNT]). It freezes when the Cortex-M0+ is halted over SWD, and cannot be frozen by software while the system domain is off.

1. Optionally switch to RCX (CLK_RCX_REG[RCX_ENABLE]). 2. Optionally freeze (SET_FREEZE_REG[FRZ_SYS_WDOG]). 3. Choose NMI/reset behaviour (NMI_RST). 4. Wait for WATCHDOG_CTRL_REG[WRITE_BUSY] = 0. 5. Allow writing (WATCHDOG_REG[WDOG_WEN] = 0). 6. Write the reload value to WDOG_VAL. 7. Resume if frozen (RESET_FREEZE_REG[FRZ_SYS_WDOG] = 1).

Present on DA14691, DA14695, DA14697 and DA14699. A USB 1.1 full-speed and low-speed device (node) controller with a serial interface engine and endpoint FIFOs, reached through pins USB_Dp and USB_Dm. Seven endpoint pipes: bidirectional control endpoint 0 with an 8-byte FIFO, three transmit and three receive endpoints with 64-byte FIFOs each. The transceiver's rise and fall times are programmable and its D+/D- pull-ups are on chip. Data PID toggling and checking and NAK packet recovery are automatic, up to 256 x 32 bytes (8 kB).

The PHY part does digital clock recovery, glitch filtering, end-of-packet detection and bit stuffing (a 0 after every six consecutive 1s) and unstuffing; the MAC part formats packets, generates and checks CRC, detects endpoint addresses and returns NAK, ACK or STALL as the endpoint pipe controller decides. It reports NodeReset, NodeSuspend and NodeResume. Output signals to the transceiver are matched within 1 ns. Clock recovery extracts 12 MHz (FS) or 1.5 MHz (LS) from the NRZI stream using a 48 MHz (FS) or 6 MHz (LS) clock, meeting chapter 7 of the USB specification.

The node supports seven endpoint pipes sharing one function address. On an IN token the pipe sends a data packet, STALL if stalled, or NAK automatically if enabled with no data (an isochronous pipe with no data sends a bit-stuff error and end of packet). On an OUT token it loads the packet into its FIFO, or answers STALL, or NAK if it has no buffer. A disabled endpoint ignores IN, OUT and SETUP. Address detection in hardware compares the token's address with FADR and its 4-bit endpoint field with the EP fields of the endpoint control registers (transmit ones for IN, receive ones for OUT); EPC0 answers IN, OUT and SETUP.

NodeOperational is normal operation. NodeSuspend: after 3 ms with no bus activity the node sets SD3 in USB_ALTEV (an interrupt if enabled) and firmware puts the node into suspend. NodeResume: a K state is driven for at least 1 ms and at most 15 ms, the host continues resume signalling for at least 20 ms more and ends with EOP. NodeReset and NodeResume detected in suspend can interrupt the CPU. Host-initiated resume raises ALTEV[RESUME] and firmware sets NodeOperational in USB_NFSR_REG. Device-initiated resume (a local event such as a key) requires at least 5 ms of idle (SD5 in USB_ALTEV) before firmware drives NodeResume through NFSR; firmware then sets NodeOperational to catch the EOP (ALTEV[EOP]) and restarts resume if no EOP comes within 100 ms. The device must answer tokens within 10 ms of wake-up or reset. All state changes are made by firmware.

Outside NodeOperational the registers hold still; only the endpoint controller state machines keep running, and the bits RX_EN, TX_EN and LAST are cleared. In NodeResume, resume signalling is sent upstream. In NodeSuspend the node may drop into low power and still detects resume signalling.

Each FIFO serves one endpoint under the single function address. Firmware must not enable both the transmit and receive FIFO for endpoint 0 at once. If two same-direction endpoints carry the same endpoint number and are both enabled, the lower-numbered one takes the data until disabled (bulk, interrupt) or full or empty (isochronous), which allows ping-pong buffering for isochronous endpoints with frame-number matching; opposite directions with the same number are independent. FIFO0 holds one packet of up to 8 bytes and can take data sent to the default address (DEF bit in EPC0); a packet stays in it and is retried at the next IN token after an error, and it can be flushed. SETUP_FIX and STALL_FIX read as 0, so a SETUP causes no state change.

The transmit FIFOs of endpoints 1, 3, 5 and the receive FIFOs of endpoints 2, 4, 6 handle bulk and interrupt packets longer than the FIFO, so firmware refills or drains them during the packet. Transmit: TXRP (read pointer, never past TXWP) and TXWP (write pointer) wrap at the FIFO size TFnS; underrun occurs if TXRP reaches TXWP with LAST in USB_TXCx_REG not set; a write beyond the free space is ignored; TXFL is the fill level and sets WARNn in FWR when at or below TFWL in TXCn; TCOUNT (in TXSn) is the free space. Receive: RXRP and RXWP wrap at RFnS; reading past the data repeats the last byte; overrun occurs if RXWP catches RXRP; RXFL is the room left and sets WARNn when at or below RFWL in RXCn; RCOUNT (in RXSn) is the bytes available.
Each event register bit is masked by its xxxMSK_REG. USBFS_IRQ goes to the CPU when a bit of MAEV_REG is set with its MAMSK_REG bit set; MAMSK_REG bit 7 is the global enable.

In NodeSuspend the transceiver drops into low power automatically. Lowest chip current comes from running from on-chip RAM or ROM (or gating external flash chip selects), putting the PLL in bypass and turning it off (CLK_CTRL_REG = 0), supplying the XTAL from AVD1 (AVD_SUPPLY = 1, default), turning off AVD_XTAL (LDO_XTAL_ON = 0), turning off the DC-DC converter, LED current and other blocks, setting BANDGAP_REG = 0x8, enabling LDO_SUSPEND and turning off the charge control. The XTAL stays on, so a clock remains for interrupts and key scanning. Any bus activity in suspend raises USB_ALTEV[RESUME]; firmware restarts the PLL and moves the system clock to it for the 48 MHz USB clock and restores what it turned off. The PLL start-up time sets how long the return to operation takes; the CPU resumes normal work once USB_NFSR is set to NodeOperational.

With SET_FREEZE_REG[FRZ_USB] set, for an in-system emulator, clear-on-read of status flags stops and the FIFOs are not updated; RESET_FREEZE_REG[FRZ_USB] = 1 releases it. The transceiver integrates the pull-up and pull-down resistors of the USB 2.0 ECN on pull-up/pull-down resistors; their switching on USB_Dp and USB_Dm can be overridden when USB_UX20CDR_REG[RPU_TEST_EN] = 1.

Present on DA14697 and DA14699 only; not on DA14691 or DA14695. Drives an LRA (linear resonant actuator) or an ERM (eccentric rotating mass) motor from a differential H-bridge output at up to 250 mA. Drive current and resonant frequency search are fully digital; the LRA resonant frequency is tracked automatically within ±20 % of the programmed value. Active acceleration and rapid stop are under software control, for short crisp bursts. It has short-circuit protection, edge-rate control for low EMI, and low consumption when idle.

The block runs from the 32 MHz system clock, divided by 16 to 2 MHz (ADC sampling) and by 128 to 250 kHz (the PWM ramp). The 250 kHz ramp is compared with LRA_CTRL3_REG[DREF] to give a variable-duty square wave for the H-bridge; LRA_CTRL2_REG[PWM_MODE] places the pulse at the start, end or middle of the period, or alternates, to shape the supply current harmonics. The drive polarity flips every LRA_CTRL2_REG[HALF_PERIOD], set in steps of 4 µs: fixed for an ERM, tracking resonance for an LRA. Edge rate and short-circuit protection of the bridge are set per side, low side in LRA_BRD_LS_REG, high side in LRA_BRD_HS_REG.

A sense resistance RS, nominally 1 Ω and varying up to ±20 % with process (to be calibrated to fix loop gain), sits on both sides of the bridge and feeds a pre-amplifier through a low-pass filter. At the 250 mA limit the sense voltage is nominally 20 mV; the pre-amplifier gain is 6, 8 (default), 10 or 12, the highest for the lowest currents, 6 and 10 for trimming the RS tolerance. A 10-bit ADC at 2 MHz gives a 16-bit signed value with eight fractional bits; the zero-current offset is removed with LRA_ADC_CTRL1_REG[LRA_ADC_OFFSET] (8-bit signed, three fractional bits). A CIC filter decimates by eight to the 250 kHz control rate. Eight samples are stored at equal spacing in each half period, D1 to D8 then D9 to D16, in LRA_FLT_SMPx_REG (x = 1 to 8). An interrupt follows the sample set by LRA_CTRL1_REG[IRQ_IDX]: 0xF interrupts after sample 16, 0x7 (default) after samples 8 and 16, for loads that behave symmetrically.

In constant-voltage drive, the LRA current is set by its series resistance R1 and modulated by the back-EMF of its parallel resonant part (L2, C1, R2); at resonance the current is a square wave with a half-sine dip in each half. Each half period the control fits a constant, a sine and a cosine to the measured current and moves the drive phase and frequency so that B = 0 with A positive (negative for fast braking). The response amplitude follows the sine term, which can feed a second loop that sets the drive strength to reach the wanted amplitude in minimum time (overdrive). The SDK software does this fit and updates HALF_PERIOD.

ERM: set the duty cycle in LRA_CTRL3_REG[DREF] for the wanted force and switch with LRA_CTRL1_REG[LRA_EN]. LRA: preset HALF_PERIOD (actuation frequency) and DREF (current amplitude and initial duty). Constant current mode is the default; constant duty mode is chosen by setting the filter coefficients LRA_FLT_COEF1/2/3_REG to 0 and choosing ADC samples with LRA_CTRL1_REG[SMP_SEL], values set to suit the actuator. LRA_EN starts the drive with current control but a fixed frequency. To track resonance, an interrupt every half cycle (about every 2.5 ms at 200 Hz) runs Cortex-M33 code that reads the stored samples and writes back the new frequency. Amplitude patterns, fast start and rapid stop are done in software.

Present on DA14697 and DA14699 only; not on DA14691 or DA14695. Two matched white LED current sinks, absolute accuracy ±5 %. Brightness is set by the sink current, eight settings from 2.5 mA in 2.5 mA steps to 20 mA (3 bits), and by PWM dimming from 0 % to 100 % duty from a timer on the low-power clock at a rate above 100 Hz; PWM works at every current setting. The reduced settings suit short pulses such as a heart-rate monitor.

A bandgap reference current is mirrored into the selected current (source fed from V30) and dropped across a 5 kΩ resistor to set the op-amp's input; the high-gain op-amp and output transistor force the same voltage across the 5 Ω output resistor, giving the selected sink current. Overvoltage protection guards the LED pins against voltages up to VBUS maximum. The drivers need bandgap bias, so they cannot run in sleep modes where the bandgap is off and only refreshed. Their control logic is in PD_PER; PD_COM can be off in sleep without affecting them.

1. PWM duty per LED in PWMLED_DUTY_CYCLE_LED1/2_REG and the shared frequency in PWMLED_FREQUENCY_REG. 2. Sink current PWMLED_CTRL_REG[LEDx_LOAD_SEL]. 3. Enable LED1_EN, LED2_EN. 4. PWM_ENABLE. Writing FRZ_PWMLED in SET_FREEZE_REG, or SW_PAUSE_EN in PWMLED_CTRL_REG, pauses the PWM.

Port 0 has 32 pins and Port 1 has 23 (counting M33_SWCLK, M33_SWDIO, CMAC_SWCLK and CMAC_SWDIO). P1_12 to P1_22 exist on DA14697 and DA14699 only, not on DA14691 or DA14695. Pin assignment is fully programmable; each pin has selectable 25 kΩ pull-up and pull-down resistors, open-drain option and a pull-up rail of V30 or V18P chosen per pin. Analog, motor controller and LCD controller pins are fixed. Pins can hold their last state in extended sleep, deep sleep and hibernation.

Px_yy_MODE_REG[5:0] maps any peripheral signal to the pin, peripheral IDs 0x00 to 0x3B. Analog, GPADC and SDADC signals are on fixed pins to limit digital interference, as are motor and LCD controller signals. M33 SWD is on P0_10 and P0_11, CMAC SWD on P0_12 and P0_13. One output may be mapped to several pins; avoiding that is up to software. If several pins feed one peripheral input, the lowest port and pin wins (P0_00 over P0_01). Direction is Px_yy_MODE_REG[9:8]; in output and analog modes the pull resistors are off.

PID = 0 selects plain GPIO. Px_DATA_REG reads the pin state at any time, also for outputs and whatever the PID, except analog mode where it reads 0; writing it sets the outputs. Writing 1s to Px_SET_OUTPUT_DATA_REG sets pins and to Px_RESET_OUTPUT_DATA_REG clears them; 0s are ignored.

Before sleep the pad states are latched so outside parts see no change and no undriven signals come from powered-down domains. Setting PAD_LATCH_EN in Px_RESET_PAD_LATCH_REG latches each pad's digital controls (input enable, open drain, data, output enable, rail select, pull-up and pull-down enables) and its output data, so a pad driving high stays high; Px_SET_PAD_LATCH_REG unlatches. After wake-up software must release the latches to control the pads again. On QSPI pads the latch is overridden by the QSPI controller as soon as its clock is enabled. A QSPI pad has a 40 kΩ resistor to ground; its latched controls are slew rate, data and drive strength.

P0_14 and P0_15 work as GPIO only with USBPAD_REG[USBPAD_EN] set, with levels of 0 V and 3 V from the V30 rail; with 1.8 V chosen as pin supply about 150 µA flows. They should not be used in sleep, since USBPAD_REG is in the system domain and these pins have no state retention. On VFBGA86, P0_18, P0_16, P1_00, P0_07, P1_09 and P0_27, and on VFBGA100, P0_16, P1_00, P1_06, P0_18, P0_06 and P0_07, can degrade the radio and the 32 MHz crystal oscillator when toggled during RF activity or while the XTAL32M runs: use them at low speed, not while the radio is active, and with weak drive as outputs where weak drive exists. P1_12, P1_18 and P1_19 can disturb the XTAL32K when toggled fast while it is in use; use them at low speed as outputs. P0_12 and P0_13 default to CMAC_SWDIO and CMAC_SWCLK and must be reprogrammed for GPIO use.

Present on DA14691, DA14695, DA14697 and DA14699. The 2.4 GHz transceiver gives a 103 dB RF link budget, -97 dBm receiver sensitivity and transmit power configurable from -18 dBm to +6 dBm, through a single-ended RFIO port matched to 50 Ω, with no alignment needed. All RF blocks are fed by on-chip LDOs with a programmable bias scheme for low power, and frequency tuning is fast. It comprises receiver, transmitter, synthesizer, RX/TX combiner and biasing LDOs.

Receive path: a selective matching network, low-noise amplifier and image-rejecting down-conversion mixer, then an IF filter with programmable gain; LNA and IF gains are under AGC; I and Q ADCs feed a digital demodulator that produces a synchronous bit stream. The synthesizer makes the quadrature LO and the modulated transmit signal: its DCO runs at twice the carrier and a divide-by-two produces the 2.4 GHz phases. The reference is the 32 MHz crystal, and transmit modulation is two-point.

The power amplifier is a Class-D stage giving typically -18 dBm to +6 dBm at the antenna, fed from the divide-by-two. The RX/TX combiner passes received power to the LNA with little loss toward the PA, and in transmit the LNA loads the PA lightly and its inputs are protected; in both modes RFIO is matched to 50 Ω for direct connection to a PCB antenna. An RF monitoring block collects demodulator I and Q data and GPADC data, packs them into 32-bit words and stores them in system memory for production testing.
The BGA packages are qualified to MSL 3. Floor life is the time a part may spend out of its dry bag, at up to 30 °C and 60 % RH, before reflow. Soldering follows JEDEC J-STD-020.
